text: AMO describes long-duration changes sea surface temperature North Atlantic Ocean characterized extended cool (negative) warm (positive) phases may last 20-60 years (Knight, Folland, Scaife 2006). heading: 15.1 Introduction to Indicator
text: Grey seal populations Atlantic Canada periodically estimated since 1960s using combination visual aerial surveys seal pups. Data region comprises one longest robust datasets pinniped abundance world. Scotian Shelf grey seal herd includes breeding populations Coastal Nova Scotia Sable Island – largest single breeding population grey seals world, source 75% Canada’s entire pup production (Heyer et al. 2024; Bowen, McMillan, Blanchard 2007).Pup production Scotian Shelf herd increased exponentially 1960s-1990s, rate increase began slow mid 2000s (Bowen, McMillan, Blanchard 2007). 2020s, population estimates appear leveling population appriaches hypothesized carrying capacity (Hammill et al. 2023).Population estimates Scotian Shelf herd produced ensembled estimates four formulations integrated population model, use different assumptions survival mortality. model uses data pup production, pregnancy rates, removals, survival, ice-related mortality rates; model consists three main components: demographic model indicating maturity--age, population dynamics model, mark-recapture model indicates survival probabilities individuals (Hammill et al. 2023).

library(plotly)

              line = list(width = 0),
              fillcolor = 'rgba(180, 180, 180, .4)',
              name = "Uncertainty Interval",
              text = ~paste0("Uncertainty Interval (1000s): ", round(lower), " - ", round(upper)),

            name = "Annual Median",

  ) %>%
  layout(yaxis = list(title = "Abundance (1000s)",
                      fixedrange = TRUE),
         xaxis = list(title = "Year"),
         hovermode = "x unified",
         title = "Grey Seal Abundance for Scotian Shelf"
  ) %>%
